text:
maya: Heads up — CI failed on publish because the `codegen/regenerate-types` step produced diffs but the release PR didn't bump semver or update CHANGELOG. p0 for a release today.

devon: I saw that. The regen diff is just type alias reorders from openapi -> tsgen. No functional change, but our publish check is strict: any diff without changelog entry blocks the pipeline.

sam: Repro steps I used: `./scripts/regen-types.sh && git status --porcelain` — shows files changed in `packages/sdk/src/generated/*`.

olga: Can we make a narrower CI rule? e.g., only block on generated API shape changes, not type formatting reorderers. Current approach causes noisy PRs.

maya: Ideally: (1) CI should detect semver-impacting changes vs purely non-semver (types-only) churn, (2) our release tooling should auto-add a changelog entry for non-user-facing regens or auto-commit a regenerate if it matches a baseline.

ci-bot: publish-check failed: codegen-diff (exit 1). See job: https://ci.redwood.ai/runs/3421

nate: Quick workaround: add a `chore(codegen): regen types` line to changelog and bump patch semver. But that's manual and noisy.

sam: Proposed fix patch (local):
```
// in scripts/check-codegen.sh
# allow non-api structural changes
if git diff --name-only | grep -E "generated/.*\.ts"; then
  if ! git diff --exit-code -- 'packages/sdk/src/generated'; then
    echo "found generated diffs"
    # run a lightweight comparator to see if only types/comments changed
    node scripts/compare-generated.js || exit 1
  fi
fi
```

devon: compare-generated.js could check AST equality ignoring comments/ts-ordering. I can prototype.

olga: Also suggests we add a CI label `regen-allowed` that maintainers can toggle on release PRs to avoid blocking hotfixes.

maya: One more friction: our OpenAPI -> OpenAPI-normalized step sometimes rewrites `nullable: true` vs `Type | null`. That triggers typegen churn. We should canonicalize earlier.

nate: +1. Fixing normalization upstream would reduce noise massively.

sam: I'll open a draft PR with the check and a test that simulates reorder-only diffs. If CI approves we can run it for a week in warn-mode (not fail) and surface counts.

devon: For semver guidance: types-only changes should be patch-only unless they alter exported runtime contracts. Let's add a short rule to RELEASES.md.

olga: I'll add an entry to onboarding docs for new contributors: "How regen diffs are handled" and include the `regen-allowed` label flow.

maya: Thanks — let's aim to have the warn-mode CI change + RELEASES.md note in by EOD so we can unstick today's release. @ci-bot can you rerun once we push the patch?

ci-bot: Re-run triggered by @maya. Job queued.

nate: small note — sample apps referencing pinned SDK types may need republishing after auto-regens. flagging product for FYI.

maya: Good call. @product please check sample-app compatibility before we auto-commit gen changes. :thumbsup:

sam: Patch PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/1298 (draft)

devon: After we stabilize, let's add a `--allow-regenerate` flag to `rwd publish` that automates changelog entry + semver patch when it's a non-user-facing regen.

maya: Solid plan. Moving to implement. Closing thread for now — follow-up in PR comments.
